    \begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-sublines}
      There exists a distribution $D$ over tuples $(\line, \line_X, \line_Z)$ with the following properties:
      \begin{enumerate}
      \item The marginal distribution over $\line$ is the same as the marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$ lying on $\line$, it holds that $u_X \in \line_X$ and $u_Z \in \line_Z$. Moreover, for $u$ chosen uniformly at random in $\line$ the marginal distribution over $(\line_X,\line_Z, u_X)$ (resp.\ over $(\line_X,\line_Z, u_Z)$) is such that the marginal over $(\ell_X,\ell_Z)$ is a mixture of $D_{\ALine, i}\times D_{\ALine, j}$ and $D_{\DLine, i}\times D_{\DLine, j}$ for $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and moreover, conditioned on $(\ell_X,\ell_Z)$, $u_X$ is uniformly random on $\line_X$ (resp. $u_Z$ uniformly random on $\line_Z$). 
\end{enumerate}
    \end{lemma}
		
    \begin{proof}
      We describe $D$ by giving a procedure to sample from it. We start by sampling $(\line, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$. Write $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$. 
	There are two cases to consider: the case where $\line$ is
        axis-parallel and the case where $\line$ is diagonal. In each case, we sample lines $\line_\xpt$ and $\line_\zpt$ such that the tuples  $(\line_\xpt,
        \line_\zpt,u_\xpt)$ and $(\line_\xpt, \line_\zpt,u_\zpt)$ satisfy Property~2 of the lemma.
        \begin{enumerate}
          \item Suppose $\line$ is an  axis-parallel line $(v,e_j)$ where
            $v = (v_\xpt,v_\zpt,\alpha_0,\beta_0)$. Then we sample $(v'_\xpt, i_\xpt), (v'_\zpt, i_\zpt) \in \F_q^m \times \{1,2, \ldots, m\}$ as described below, and set $\line_\xpt =
            (v'_\xpt,e_{i_\xpt}),\line_\zpt = (v'_\zpt, e_{i_\zpt})$.
            \begin{enumerate}
              \item If $1 \leq j \leq m$, then set $i_\xpt = j$ and
                choose $i_\zpt$ to be uniformly random in $\{1, \dots,
                m\}$.
              \item If  $m+1 \leq j \leq 2m$, then set $i_\xpt$ to be
                uniformly random in $\{1, \dots, m\}$ and $i_\zpt = j - m$.
              \item If $2m + 1 \leq j \leq 2m+2$, then set $i_\xpt$
                and $i_\zpt$ to both be uniformly random in $\{1, \dots, m\}$.
              \item Let $v'_\xpt$ be the canonical representative
                $L_{e_{i_\xpt}}^\lnf(v_\xpt)$, and
                likewise let $v'_\zpt$ be the canonical
                representative $L_{e_{i_\zpt}}^\lnf(v_{\zpt})$ (see
                \Cref{def:line-representative} for the definition of
                the canonical representative of a line). Note that
                $v_\xpt$ lies on the line $\line_\xpt = (v'_\xpt,
                e_{i_\xpt})$, and similarly for $v_\zpt$ and
                $\line_{\zpt} = (v'_\zpt, e_{i_\zpt})$.
              \end{enumerate}
              We claim that this construction satisfies Property~2 of the lemma. We show this first $(\line_X,\line_Z)$ and $u_X$, the other case being symmetric. If we are in case (a), then $u_X$ is a uniformly random point on the line $\line_X=(v_X, e_j)$ and $\line_Z=(v_Z,e_{i_Z})$, which is independent from $\line_X$. Thus, the marginal distribution over $(\line_X,u_X)$ conditioned on $j$ in this case is equal to $D_{\ALine, j}$ and furthermore even conditioned on $(\line_X,u_X)$, $\line_Z$ is distributed according to $D_{\ALine,i_Z}$ for a uniformly random $i_Z$. Cases (b) and (c) are analogous except that in this case even conditioned on $j$, $i_X$ is uniform. 
      \item Suppose $\ell$ is a random diagonal line $(v, s, w)$,
        where $v = (v_\xpt, v_\zpt, \alpha, \beta)$, and
        where $w = (w_\xpt, w_\zpt, \gamma, \delta) $ is a direction vector whose first nonzero coordinate is
         $j = \chi(s)$ (where $\chi$ is defined in \Cref{eq:chi-func}). We sample $\line_\xpt =  (v'_\xpt, s_\xpt,
        w'_\xpt)$ and $\line_\zpt = (v'_\zpt, s_\zpt, w'_\zpt)$ in the following
        manner:
        \begin{enumerate}
          \item If $1 \leq j \leq m$, then $w'_\xpt = w_\xpt$ and $w'_\zpt = w_\zpt$. We choose $s_\xpt$ and $s_\zpt$ such that $\chi(s_\xpt) = j$ and $\chi(s_\zpt) = 1$.
          \item If $m+1 \leq j \leq 2m$, then $w'_\xpt$ is a random
            diagonal line direction (and $s_{\xpt}$ is chosen accordingly), and $w'_\zpt = w_\zpt$, with $s_\zpt$ such that $\chi(s_\zpt) = j - m$.
          \item If $2m+1 \leq j \leq 2m+2$ then both $w_\xpt$, and
            $w_\zpt$ are uniformly random, with $s_\xpt$ and $s_\zpt$ chosen accordingly.
          \item Set $v'_\xpt = L_{w'_{\xpt}}^\lnf(v_\xpt)$ and $v'_\zpt = L_{w'_{\zpt}}^\lnf(v_\zpt)$.
          \end{enumerate}
          We claim that this construction satisfies Property~2 of the Lemma. We show this first $(\line_X,\line_Z)$ and $u_X$, the other case being symmetric.  If we are in case (a), then $u_X$ is a uniformly random point on the diagonal line $(v_X, s_X, w_X)$ which is equal to $\line_X$. Thus, the marginal distribution over $(\line_X, u_X)$ conditioned on $j$ in this case is equal to $D_{\DLine, j}$. Furthermore, conditioned on $(\line_X,u_X)$, $\line_Z$ is distributed according to $D_{\DLine,1}$. The other cases can be analyed analogously, with the only difference being how the indices $i,j$ of $\line_X$ and $\line_Z$ distributions are chosen. 
					    \end{enumerate}
	Let $D$ be the distribution over tuples $(\line, \line_X, \line_Z)$ induced by this procedure. This distribution $D$ satisfies Property 1 in the lemma by  construction, and Property 2 as argued above.
    \end{proof}

    26	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    28	The canonical representative map is blueprint
    29	`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
    30	blueprint `def:combine-map`.

    41	/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
    42	
    43	/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
    44	`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
    45	is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    47	-/
    48	theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    49	    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
    50	  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
    51	  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
    52	  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
    53	  exact h.symm
    54	
    55	/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
    56	
    57	/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
    58	canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
    59	the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
    60	`q` elements: for a nonzero direction the parameter is determined and the
    61	representative varies over a coset of the span of the direction, and for the
    62	zero direction the representative is the point itself and the parameter is
    63	free.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    65	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul {K : Type*} [Field K]
    66	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) :
    67	    (uniformDistribution ((Fin m → K) × K)).map
    68	        (fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) =
    69	      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
    70	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card K) fun x => ?_
    71	  by_cases hv : v = 0
    72	  · subst hv
    73	    have hfilter :
    74	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    75	            fun w => lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) w.1 + w.2 • (0 : Fin m → K)
    76	              = x)
    77	          = ({x} : Finset (Fin m → K)) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset K) := by
    78	      ext w
    79	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
    80	        Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton, and_true, smul_zero,
    81	        add_zero, lineRepMap_zero_apply]
    82	    rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
    83	    simp
    84	  · have hinj : Function.Injective
    85	        (fun c : K => (lineRepMap v x + c • v, directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    86	      intro c₁ c₂ hc
    87	      have hc' : c₁ • v = c₂ • v := by
    88	        have h := congrArg Prod.fst hc
    89	        simpa using h
    90	      have hsub : (c₁ - c₂) • v = 0 := by
    91	        rw [sub_smul, hc', sub_self]
    92	      rcases smul_eq_zero.mp hsub with h | h
    93	      · exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
    94	      · exact absurd h hv
    95	    have himg :
    96	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    97	            fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v = x)
    98	          = (Finset.univ : Finset K).image
    99	              (fun c => (lineRepMap v x + c • v,
   100	                directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
   101	      ext w
   102	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image]
   103	      constructor
   104	      · intro hw
   105	        have hrep : lineRepMap v w.1 = lineRepMap v x := by
   106	          rw [← hw, lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   107	        have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + w.2 • v := by
   108	          rw [← hrep]
   109	          exact hw.symm
   110	        have ht : directLineRepParameter v x = w.2 :=
   111	          directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv hx
   112	        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp
   113	          (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v w.1)
   114	        refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   115	        have hw1 : lineRepMap v x + c • v = w.1 := by
   116	          rw [← hrep, hc]
   117	          abel
   118	        rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   119	        exact ⟨hw1, ht⟩
   120	      · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
   121	        show lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v x + c • v) +
   122	          directLineRepParameter v x • v = x
   123	        rw [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   124	        exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v x).symm
   125	    rw [himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj, Finset.card_univ]
   126	
   127	/-- Averaged form of the previous identity: on the uniform coordinate space a
   128	quantity of the canonical representative of the point and of the point itself
   129	has the same average as the quantity of the representative and of the point at
   130	an independent uniform affine parameter on the line through it.  This is the
   131	direction-agnostic resampling step shared by the axis and diagonal line-point
   132	samplers; it uses no property of the direction, and in particular holds for the
   133	zero direction.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   134	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`, used
   135	at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`. -/
   136	theorem avgOver_uniformDistribution_lineRepMap_resample {K : Type*} [Field K]
   137	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K)
   138	    (quantity : (Fin m → K) → (Fin m → K) → ℝ) :
   139	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K))
   140	        (fun point => quantity (lineRepMap v point) point) =
   141	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K)) (fun point =>
   142	        avgOver (uniformDistribution K) (fun param =>
   143	          quantity (lineRepMap v point) (lineRepMap v point + param • v))) := by
   144	  have hmap := uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul v
   145	  have havg := congrArg (fun dist => avgOver dist
   146	    (fun point => quantity (lineRepMap v point) point)) hmap
   147	  rw [Distribution.avgOver_map, uniformDistribution_prod, avgOver_prod] at havg
   148	  simpa only [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self] using havg.symm
   149	
   150	/-! ## Injectivity of the two block embeddings -/
   151	
   152	/-- The `X`-block coordinate embedding of `def:combine-map` is injective.
   153	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
   154	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   155	theorem embX_injective (m : ℕ) : Function.Injective (embX m) := by
   156	  intro i j hij
   157	  simpa using (finCombineEquiv m).symm.injective hij
   158	
   159	/-- The `Z`-block coordinate embedding of `def:combine-map` is injective.
   160	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
   161	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   162	theorem embZ_injective (m : ℕ) : Function.Injective (embZ m) := by
   163	  intro i j hij
   164	  simpa using (finCombineEquiv m).symm.injective hij

     4	/-!
     5	# Axis line-point parameter resampling
     6	
     7	This module records that a uniformly sampled point on an axis-parallel line
     8	may be resampled by an independent uniform affine parameter without changing
     9	the joint line-point expectation.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The resampling is used at
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955`; the
    15	axis line-point law is `def:line-point-dist` at
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Resampling a uniform affine parameter on the sampled axis line preserves
    26	the joint axis line-point law. This is the axis case of the conditional
    27	sampling used at paper line 955. -/
    28	theorem avgOver_aLinePointDist_resample_parameter (L : LdParams)
    29	    (value : (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) → ℝ) :
    30	    avgOver (aLinePointDist L) value =
    31	    avgOver (aLinePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    32	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    33	        value (sample.1, sample.1.base + param • sample.1.direction))) := by
    34	  classical
    35	  unfold aLinePointDist clDistribution
    36	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map, aLineDescOf_ldALineCL]
    37	  have hblock := uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm
    38	  rw [← hblock]
    39	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map]
    40	  rw [uniformDistribution_prod]
    41	  simp only [avgOver_prod]
    42	  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))]
    43	  apply congrArg
    44	  funext block
    45	  let direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    46	    coordinateDirection (chiIndex L block.1)
    47	  change avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    48	      value (LineDesc.axis (lineRepMap direction point) block.1
    49	        (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point), point)) =
    50	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    51	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    52	        value (LineDesc.axis (lineRepMap direction point) block.1
    53	          (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point),
    54	          lineRepMap direction point + param • direction)))
    55	  have haxis := avgOver_uniformDistribution_lineRepMap_resample direction
    56	    (fun base point => value (LineDesc.axis
    57	      (lineRepMap direction base) block.1
    58	      (lineRepMap_apply_self _ _), point))
    59	  simpa only [lineRepMap_apply_self] using haxis
    60	
    61	end

    63	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Diagonal line-point parameter resampling
     6	
     7	This module proves that a uniform affine parameter may replace the sampled
     8	point on a diagonal line without changing the joint diagonal line-point law,
     9	including its zero-direction fibers.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The result supports the Schwartz-Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`, for
    15	the diagonal sampler of
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    17	-/

    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Resampling a uniform parameter on the sampled diagonal line preserves the
    26	joint line-point law, including the zero-direction fibers. This
    27	formalization-only identity derives the conditional sampling used at paper
    28	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955` from `def:line-point-dist`. -/
    29	theorem avgOver_dLinePointDist_resample_parameter (L : LdParams)
    30	    (value : (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) -> ℝ) :
    31	    avgOver (dLinePointDist L) value =
    32	      avgOver (dLinePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    33	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    34	          value (sample.1, sample.1.base + param • sample.1.direction))) := by
    35	  classical
    36	  unfold dLinePointDist clDistribution
    37	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map, dLineDescOf_ldDLineCL]
    38	  have hblock := uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm
    39	  rw [← hblock]
    40	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map]
    41	  rw [uniformDistribution_prod]
    42	  simp only [avgOver_prod]
    43	  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L))]
    44	  apply congrArg
    45	  funext block
    46	  let direction : Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L :=
    47	    prefixProjection (chiIndex L block.1) block.2
    48	  have hprefix : ∀ index : Fin L.m, index.val < (chiIndex L block.1).val ->
    49	      direction index = 0 := by
    50	    intro index hindex
    51	    simp [direction, prefixProjection, hindex]
    52	  change avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    53	      value (LineDesc.diagonal (lineRepMap direction point) block.1 direction
    54	        (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point) hprefix, point)) =
    55	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    56	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    57	        value (LineDesc.diagonal (lineRepMap direction point) block.1 direction
    58	          (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point) hprefix,
    59	          lineRepMap direction point + param • direction)))
    60	  have h := avgOver_uniformDistribution_lineRepMap_resample direction
    61	    (fun base point => value (LineDesc.diagonal
    62	      (lineRepMap direction base) block.1 direction
    63	      (lineRepMap_apply_self direction base) hprefix, point))
    64	  simpa only [lineRepMap_apply_self] using h
    65	
    66	end
